faqs.question: What is Net Metering?
faqs.answer: Net metering is a billing arrangement that allows solar system owners to send excess electricity back to the national grid. Your electricity meter runs backward when you produce more than you use, reducing your WAPDA/LESCO bill or earning credits. In Pakistan, net metering is regulated by NEPRA.

faqs.question: What is an On-Grid Solar System?
faqs.answer: An on-grid (grid-tied) solar system is connected to the national electricity grid. It uses solar power during the day and draws from the grid at night. On-grid systems qualify for net metering but do not provide power during load-shedding unless paired with battery backup.

faqs.question: What is a Hybrid Solar System?
faqs.answer: A hybrid solar system combines solar panels with battery storage and remains connected to the grid. It stores excess energy in batteries for use during load-shedding or at night, providing uninterrupted power supply (UPS) functionality along with the bill savings of solar.

faqs.question: What are Tier-1 Solar Panels?
faqs.answer: Tier-1 solar panels come from manufacturers with a proven 5+ year track record, strong financial ratings, and fully automated production processes. They offer the highest reliability, consistent output, and the strongest long-term warranties. Solarlink uses only Tier-1 panels including Canadian Solar.

faqs.question: How much does a residential solar system cost in Pakistan?
faqs.answer: A residential solar system in Pakistan typically costs between PKR 8–25 lakh depending on system size (5–15kW). A 10kW on-grid system costs approximately PKR 12–16 lakh installed. SolarLink provides free site surveys and custom proposals with no obligation.

faqs.question: What size solar system do I need for my home?
faqs.answer: For most homes in Punjab with monthly bills of PKR 20,000–50,000, a 5–10kW system is recommended. For bills above PKR 50,000, a 10–15kW system may be needed. SolarLink engineers assess your consumption, roof space, and budget to recommend the ideal size.

faqs.question: How long does residential solar installation take?
faqs.answer: Typical residential installation takes 1–3 days. The complete process from inquiry to commissioning — including site survey, design, procurement, and installation — takes approximately 2–4 weeks.

faqs.question: Will I really get a zero electricity bill?
faqs.answer: With a correctly sized on-grid or hybrid solar system, your net metered bill can drop to near zero or generate credits. Many SolarLink customers in Lahore, Islamabad, Rawalpindi, and Sargodha report monthly bills under PKR 1,000 after installation.

faqs.question: What happens to my solar system during load-shedding?
faqs.answer: A standard on-grid system shuts down during load-shedding for safety. To maintain power during outages, a hybrid system with battery storage is recommended. SolarLink can help you choose the right option for your needs and budget.

faqs.question: Does SolarLink help with net metering for residential customers?
faqs.answer: Yes. SolarLink handles the complete net metering application process for LESCO, IESCO, MEPCO, and GEPCO — from documentation to DISCO inspection to bi-directional meter installation.

faqs.question: What warranty does SolarLink provide?
faqs.answer: SolarLink provides a 2-year workmanship warranty on all installations. Growatt inverters come with 5-year standard warranty (extendable to 10) and Canadian Solar panels carry a 25-year linear power output warranty.

faqs.question: How many solar panels do I need for my home?
faqs.answer: For an average Pakistani home paying PKR 20,000–30,000 per month in electricity, a 5kW to 8kW system (10–16 panels) is typically sufficient. Homes with 3+ air conditioners usually need 10kW or more. A free site survey gives the exact recommendation.

faqs.question: What is the payback period for solar in Pakistan?
faqs.answer: The typical payback period for solar in Pakistan is 3 to 4 years. After that, you enjoy essentially free electricity for the remaining 20+ years of your system's life. Rising electricity tariffs are making payback periods shorter every year.

faqs.question: Will my solar system work during load-shedding?
faqs.answer: On-grid solar systems automatically shut down during load-shedding for safety. For uninterrupted power, Solarlink recommends a hybrid system with battery backup, which keeps your home powered even when the grid is down.

faqs.question: Does Solarlink provide after-sales support?
faqs.answer: Yes. Solarlink provides a 1-year warranty on all installation work and offers ongoing maintenance and after-sales support. Our team is reachable by phone or WhatsApp from offices across Lahore, Islamabad, Rawalpindi, and Sargodha.

faqs.question: Can I get net metering for my home solar system?
faqs.answer: Yes. Any grid-connected solar system above 1kW qualifies for net metering in Pakistan. Solarlink handles the full application process with WAPDA/LESCO on your behalf. Approval typically takes 4–8 weeks.

faqs.question: How many solar panels do I need for a 3-bedroom house in Pakistan?
faqs.answer: A 3-bedroom house in Pakistan with 2 air conditioners typically requires a 6kW to 8kW system — approximately 12 to 16 panels of 580W each. Homes with larger load profiles or 3+ ACs may need 10kW. Solarlink provides a free site survey to calculate the exact requirement.

faqs.question: Can solar panels run AC in Pakistan?
faqs.answer: Yes. Solar panels can run air conditioners in Pakistan. A 1.5-ton AC consumes approximately 1.5kW per hour. A 10kW solar system can comfortably run 4–6 air conditioners simultaneously during peak sun hours. Hybrid systems with battery backup also power ACs during load-shedding.

faqs.question: What is the best solar system for home in Pakistan?
faqs.answer: For most Pakistani homes, a hybrid solar system with net metering is the best option. It reduces bills by 70–100% using net metering, and the battery backup keeps your home powered during load-shedding. Solarlink recommends Growatt hybrid inverters with Canadian Solar Tier-1 panels for maximum reliability.

faqs.question: What size commercial solar system do I need?

faqs.question: Can I get net metering for my business?
faqs.answer: Yes. Commercial properties in Pakistan are fully eligible for net metering under NEPRA regulations. SolarLink handles the complete net metering application process for your business.

faqs.question: How long does commercial solar installation take?
faqs.answer: Commercial installations typically take 3–10 days depending on system size and complexity. The full project — from survey to commissioning — takes approximately 3–6 weeks.

faqs.question: Is commercial solar suitable for rented business premises?
faqs.answer: Solar can be installed on rented premises with the landlord's written consent. Many businesses negotiate this into their lease. SolarLink can advise on the legal and practical considerations for your specific situation.

faqs.question: What happens to business operations during installation?
faqs.answer: SolarLink schedules commercial installations to minimise disruption — typically during off-hours or weekends. Grid power remains active throughout. A brief 1–2 hour outage is only needed for final grid connection.

faqs.question: How much can a business save with solar in Pakistan?
faqs.answer: Businesses with monthly bills of PKR 100,000+ typically see savings of 70–90% after installing solar. A 25kW commercial system can save a business over PKR 1,000,000 per year, with full payback in 3–4 years.

faqs.question: What size solar system does a commercial building need?

faqs.question: Is solar viable for businesses in Pakistan given frequent load-shedding?
faqs.answer: Yes. A hybrid commercial solar system with battery backup provides continuous power even during load-shedding. This eliminates reliance on expensive diesel generators, reducing both fuel costs and downtime.

faqs.question: Does net metering apply to commercial solar systems?
faqs.answer: Yes. Commercial solar systems qualify for net metering in Pakistan. Businesses can sell excess electricity back to WAPDA/LESCO during peak generation hours and draw from the grid at night, significantly reducing net bills.

faqs.question: How long does commercial solar installation take?
faqs.answer: Commercial solar installations by Solarlink typically take 1 to 2 weeks depending on system size and site conditions. We handle all permitting, civil work, electrical work, and net metering paperwork.

faqs.question: What does kW or kWp mean?
faqs.answer: kWp (Kilowatt Peak) is the unit used to measure solar system size. It refers to the maximum power output under ideal sunlight conditions. A 10kWp system produces approximately 40–50 units (kWh) of electricity per day in Pakistan's climate.

faqs.question: How does agricultural solar work for tubewells in Pakistan?
faqs.answer: Agricultural solar systems power irrigation tubewells directly from solar panels, eliminating WAPDA electricity costs entirely. The system is sized based on your tubewell motor capacity (typically 7.5–30HP). On sunny days, the pump runs on solar; a hybrid system can add battery backup or grid connection for cloudy days.

faqs.question: What is the cost of a solar tubewell system in Pakistan?
faqs.answer: A solar tubewell system for a 10HP motor typically costs PKR 8–15 lakh depending on panel brand and system type. The payback period is usually 2–4 years given the high cost of agricultural electricity in Pakistan.

faqs.question: Does SolarLink serve rural areas for agricultural solar?
faqs.answer: Yes. SolarLink serves agricultural customers across Punjab including areas around Lahore, Sargodha, and surrounding rural districts. Contact our Sargodha office (048-3720111) for agricultural enquiries in central Punjab.

faqs.question: Can agricultural solar systems run at night or during cloudy weather?
faqs.answer: Standard on-grid agricultural systems only run during daylight. For night or cloudy-day operation, a hybrid system with battery storage or net metering can provide continuous power. SolarLink's engineers will help you select the best solution for your farming needs.

faqs.question: What is a VFD solar pump system and how is it different?
faqs.answer: A VFD (Variable Frequency Drive) solar pump system uses a drive to control motor speed based on available solar power — making it more efficient in partially cloudy conditions compared to standard direct-coupled systems. SolarLink recommends VFD-based systems for most agricultural applications.

faqs.question: Can I get net metering for an agricultural solar system?
faqs.answer: Agricultural consumers connected to the grid are eligible for net metering under NEPRA regulations. SolarLink can install a net-metered agricultural system so that any surplus power generated during low-irrigation periods earns bill credits.

faqs.question: How much does a solar tubewell system cost in Pakistan?
faqs.answer: A solar tubewell system in Pakistan typically costs between PKR 400,000 and PKR 1,200,000 depending on pump size and depth. The system pays for itself within 2–3 years by eliminating diesel and electricity costs.

faqs.question: Can solar panels run a tubewell 24 hours a day?
faqs.answer: Solar tubewells run during daylight hours (6–10 hours per day depending on season). For 24-hour operation, a battery backup or hybrid system is required. Most farmers find daytime operation sufficient for irrigation needs.

faqs.question: What is the best solar system size for a tubewell in Punjab?
faqs.answer: Most agricultural tubewells in Punjab require a 7.5HP to 15HP motor, which needs a 7kW to 15kW solar system. Solarlink provides free site surveys to recommend the exact system size for your tubewell and crop requirements.

faqs.question: Does agricultural solar work on cloudy days in Punjab?
faqs.answer: Yes. Solar panels still generate 15–25% of peak power on cloudy days. Punjab averages over 300 sunny days per year, making solar highly reliable for agricultural use throughout most crop seasons.

faqs.question: Does Solarlink install solar tubewells in rural Punjab?
faqs.answer: Yes. Solarlink installs agricultural solar and tubewell systems across Punjab including Sargodha, Lahore, and surrounding areas. Call our Sargodha office at 048-3720111 for agricultural solar consultations.

faqs.question: What is net metering in Pakistan?
faqs.answer: Net metering is a NEPRA-approved policy that allows solar system owners to export surplus electricity back to the national grid (WAPDA/LESCO/IESCO etc.) and receive credits on their electricity bill. When your system generates more than you need, you effectively sell it back — reducing or eliminating your bill.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for net metering in Pakistan?
faqs.answer: Any consumer with a grid-connected solar system (1kW to 1MW) is eligible for net metering in Pakistan. Residential, commercial, and industrial consumers can all apply. The system must be properly installed and inspected by a licensed solar company.

faqs.question: How long does the net metering approval take in Pakistan?
faqs.answer: The net metering approval process from distribution companies (LESCO, IESCO, MEPCO, etc.) typically takes 4–12 weeks. SolarLink handles the complete application, documentation, and follow-up on your behalf.

faqs.question: What documents are needed for a net metering application?
faqs.answer: Required documents include: CNIC copy, electricity bill copy, property documents, single-line diagram, equipment specifications, commissioner/notary affidavit, and inspection certificate from SolarLink. We handle all documentation for our customers.

faqs.question: Can I apply for net metering myself or do I need SolarLink?
faqs.answer: You can apply independently, but working with a licensed installer like SolarLink is strongly recommended. We manage the complete process — from design approval to DISCO inspection to meter replacement — saving you months of paperwork and repeated follow-up visits.

faqs.question: Does net metering work with LESCO, IESCO, MEPCO, and GEPCO?
faqs.answer: Yes. Net metering is available under all major electricity distribution companies in Pakistan including LESCO (Lahore), IESCO (Islamabad), MEPCO (Multan/Faisalabad), and GEPCO (Gujranwala). SolarLink has experience handling applications across all of these DISCOs.

faqs.question: What is a bi-directional meter and why do I need one?
faqs.answer: A bi-directional meter records both the electricity you consume from the grid and the surplus electricity you export back. It replaces your standard meter and is installed by the DISCO as part of the net metering approval process. SolarLink coordinates the meter replacement on your behalf.
